{{Short description|Mathematical optimization function}}
The '''Moreau envelope''' (or the Moreau-Yosida regularization) <math>M_f</math> of a proper [[Semi-continuity|lower semi-continuous]] [[convex function]] <math>f</math> is a smoothed version of <math>f</math>. It was proposed by [[Jean-Jacques Moreau]] in 1965.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Moreau |first=J. J. |date=1965 |title=Proximité et dualité dans un espace hilbertien |url=https://eudml.org/doc/87067 |journal=Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France |volume=93 |pages=273–299 |doi=10.24033/bsmf.1625 |issn=0037-9484|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The Moreau envelope has important applications in [[mathematical optimization]]: minimizing over <math>M_f</math> and minimizing over <math>f</math> are equivalent problems in the sense that the sets of minimizers of <math>f</math>  and <math>M_f</math> are the same. However, first-order optimization algorithms can be directly applied to <math>M_f</math>, since <math>f</math> may be non-differentiable while <math>M_f</math> is always continuously differentiable. Indeed, many [[proximal gradient method]]s can be interpreted as a [[gradient descent]] method over <math>M_f</math>.

== Definition ==
The Moreau envelope of a proper lower semi-continuous convex function <math>f</math> from a [[Hilbert space]] <math>\mathcal{X}</math> to <math>(-\infty,+\infty]</math> is defined as<ref name=":0">{{cite journal |author=Neal Parikh and Stephen Boyd |year=2013 |title=Proximal Algorithms |url=https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/pdf/prox_algs.pdf |journal=Foundations and Trends in Optimization |volume=1 |issue=3 |pages=123–231 |access-date=2019-01-29}}</ref>

<math>M_{f}(v) = \inf_{x\in\mathcal{X}} \left(f(x) + \frac{1}{2} \|x - v\|_2^2\right).</math>

Given a parameter <math>\lambda \in \mathbb{R}</math>, the Moreau envelope of <math>\lambda f</math> is also called as the Moreau envelope of <math>f</math> with parameter <math>\lambda</math>.<ref name=":0" />

== Properties ==
* The Moreau envelope can also be seen as the [[infimal convolution]] between <math>f</math> and <math>(1/2)\| \cdot \|^2_2</math>.
* The [[proximal operator]] of a function is related to the gradient of the Moreau envelope by the following identity:
<math>\nabla M_{\lambda f}(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda} (x - \mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f}(x))</math>. By defining the sequence <math>x_{k+1} = \mathrm{prox}_{\lambda f}(x_k)</math> and using the above identity, we can interpret the proximal operator as a gradient descent algorithm over the Moreau envelope.

* Using [[Fenchel's duality theorem]], one can derive the following dual formulation of the Moreau envelope: 
<math display="block">M_{\lambda f}(v) = \max_{p \in \mathcal X} \left( \langle p, v \rangle - \frac{\lambda}{2} \| p \|^2 - f^*(p)\right),</math> where <math>f^*</math> denotes the [[convex conjugate]] of <math>f</math>.
Since the subdifferential of a proper, convex, lower semicontinuous function on a Hilbert space is inverse to the subdifferential of its convex conjugate, we can conclude that if <math>p_0 \in \mathcal X</math> is the maximizer of the above expression, then <math>x_0 := v - \lambda p_0</math> is the minimizer in the primal formulation and vice versa.

* By [[Hopf–Lax formula]], the Moreau envelope is a [[viscosity solution]] to a [[Hamilton–Jacobi equation]].<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last1=Heaton |first1=Howard |last2=Fung |first2=Samy Wu |last3=Osher |first3=Stanley |date=2022-10-09 |title=Global Solutions to Nonconvex Problems by Evolution of Hamilton–Jacobi PDEs |class=math.OC |eprint=2202.11014 }}</ref> [[Stanley Osher]] and co-authors used this property and [[Cole–Hopf transformation]] to derive an algorithm to compute approximations to the proximal operator of a function.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Osher |first1=Stanley |last2=Heaton |first2=Howard |last3=Fung |first3=Samy Wu |date=2023 |title=A Hamilton–Jacobi-based proximal operator |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=120 |issue=14 |article-number=e2220469120 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2220469120 |doi-access=free |pmid=36989305 |pmc=10083605 |arxiv=2211.12997 |bibcode=2023PNAS..12020469O }}</ref>
